4Q129 f1R:1.en: I am speaking in the ears on this day, and you have learned the signs and you have kept to do them: Yahweh our God has made with us
4Q129 f1R:1.notes: The translation incorporates high-confidence phrase evidence for 'I am speaking in the ears on this day' and 'Yahweh our God has made with us'. The sequence 'you have learned the signs and you have kept to do them' is a paraphrase supported by repeated phrase evidence. Uncertainty in the source is not reflected in the translation per instructions, but the notes acknowledge the presence of uncertain and reconstructed elements.

4Q129 f1R:2.en: The covenant in Horeb: not our fathers did YHWH make this covenant, but with us who are alive here today. Face to face YHWH spoke with you on the mountain from the midst of the fire. And I stand between YHWH and you now.
4Q129 f1R:2.notes: Positions 33-34: uncertain reconstruction of preposition and noun. Position 39: uncertain reconstruction of pronoun.

4Q129 f1R:3.en: At that time, to tell you the word of YHWH: you feared because of the fire, and did not ascend the mountain, saying: I am YHWH your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from a house of slaves.
4Q129 f1R:3.notes: Positions 24, 36: Untranslated punctuation mark. Position 26: Uncertain reconstruction.

4Q129 f1R:4.en: Let there be no other gods before you. Do not make for yourself an idol, any form that is in the heavens above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the waters under the earth. Do not bow down to them and do not serve them, for I am
4Q129 f1R:4.notes: Uncertainty in the transcription affects the translation of 'bow down' (position 35), 'to' (position 36), and 'serve' (position 39). The phrase 'for I am' is incomplete due to damage at the end of the line.

4Q129 f1R:5.en: YHWH, your gods, [am] a jealous God who visits the sin of [the] fathers upon [the] sons, and upon [the] grandsons, and upon a fourth generation of those who hate me. And [he] makes covenant loyalty to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments. You shall not lift up the name of YHWH your God to vanity, for YHWH will not leave unpunished the one who lifts up his name to vanity.
4Q129 f1R:5.notes: Uncertain reconstruction at positions 29 and 41. Phrase evidence supports renderings for positions 3-6, 15-17, 21-23, 23-25, 33-35, and 34-35. Semantic constraints do not apply.

4Q129 f1R:6.en: YHWH carries the name for vanity. Keep the day of the sabbath to be holy, as YHWH your God commanded. Six days you will labor and do all work. And on the seventh day, a sabbath to YHWH your God.
4Q129 f1R:6.notes: Positions 25-27, 30, 32-35, and 39 contain uncertain or damaged text. Positions 9, 22, and 31 contain untranslatable punctuation.

4Q129 f1R:7.en: Do not do any work, you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, your bullock, your he-ass, all your cattle, and the sojourner within your gates, so that your male servant and your female servant may rest like you.
4Q129 f1R:7.notes: Uncertain elements: verb form at position 27 (י?נוח), damaged suffix at position 30 (א##מת׳כה), reconstructed preposition at position 31 (כמ##[ ו׳כה), and particle at position 35 (כי#?). 4Q129 f1R:8.en: You were a servant in the land of Egypt, and Yahweh your God brought you out from there by a strong hand and by an arm outstretched. Thus Yahweh your God commanded you to make the day of the sabbath holy. Honor your father and your mother.
4Q129 f1R:8.notes: Positions 23, 31, 37: Uncertain reconstruction. Position 32: Untranslated punctuation.

4Q129 f1R:9.en: As YHWH your God commanded, so that your days may be long and that it may go well for you upon the land which YHWH your God gave you: Do not kill. And do not commit adultery. And do not steal. And do not bear false witness against your neighbor. And do not desire.
4Q129 f1R:9.notes: Positions 23, 31, 33-35, and 42 contain uncertain text. Position 21 contains an untranslatable surviving source character.

4Q129 f1R:11.en: Great, and he did not add, and he wrote them on two tablets of stone, and he gave them to him. And it was as they heard the sound from the midst of the darkness and the mountain burning with fire, and they approached to all the heads of the tribes and the elders. And they said?
4Q129 f1R:11.notes: Uncertainty in the transcription affects the translation of several words: 'burn' (position 29), 'and' (position 41), and 'say' (position 42). The phrase 'two tablets of stone' is supported by repeated evidence. The phrase 'the mountain [was] burning' is also supported by repeated evidence, but the exact wording is uncertain due to damage. The translation of 'heads' (position 36) is uncertain due to damage. The final 'and they said?' is highly uncertain due to extensive damage.

4Q129 f1R:12.en: And you approached to all the chiefs of your tribes and the elders, and you said, 'Behold, we have seen Yahweh.'
4Q129 f1R:12.notes: The translation includes reconstructed and uncertain elements. The phrase 'to all' is supported by repeated evidence. 'The chiefs your tribes' is a contextual rendering with moderate support. 'YHWH' is rendered as 'Yahweh' based on standard practice.

4Q129 f1R:13.en: [God's] weight and greatness and sound we heard from the midst of the fire. On this day we have seen that God spoke to the man and lived. And now, why should we die, because she consumed the great fire?
4Q129 f1R:13.notes: Positions 27, 30, 34, 38, and 39 are uncertain. Positions 1 and 44 are reconstructed.

4Q129 f1R:14.en: We, to hear the voice of Yahweh our God, still and we died. For who is all flesh that heard the voice of the living God speaking from the midst of the fire like us and lived? Approach, you, and hear all that Yahweh says.
4Q129 f1R:14.notes: The phrase 'still and we died' reflects uncertainty in the reconstruction of 'עוד ומתנו'. The phrase 'the living God' is a paraphrase of 'אלהים חיים' based on repeated phrase evidence. The phrase 'like us' is a paraphrase of 'כמונו' based on repeated phrase evidence. The phrase 'approach, you, and hear all that Yahweh says' reflects uncertainty in the reconstruction of 'קרב אתה ושמע את כל'. The phrase 'the voice of Yahweh our God' is a paraphrase of 'קול יהוה אלהינו' based on repeated phrase evidence.

4Q129 f1R:17.en: It will be good for them, the sons for eternity. Go, say to them, 'Return to your tents.' And you, stand here, and I will speak to you all the commandment, the statutes, and the judgments that you were taught.

Uncertainty in the transcription is noted for positions 24, 26, and 27, but the translation reflects the recoverable text. No unsupported elements were added, and all recoverable words are included.
